prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your budget, the size/age of your house and ducts, the brand you want, how quickly you need the job done, and whether you prioritize lowest price or longest warranty and best service. I can, however, give you a practical plan to find the best Atlanta contractor for your AC replacement and what to look for when comparing bids.

Quick plan
- Get at least 3 written estimates from reputable local contractors.
- Require a Manual J load calculation (right size unit for your home).
- Compare like-for-like proposals (same capacity, SEER, brand, warranties, and scope).
- Choose the contractor with a clear, itemized proposal and good references — not necessarily the lowest price.

How to find reputable Atlanta contractors
- Search for local companies with many recent 4–5 star reviews on Google/Angi/Yelp and an A rating from BBB.
- Prefer NATE-certified technicians and ACCA or manufacturer (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, etc.) dealer status.
- Confirm Georgia HVAC license/permit capability and company insurance.
- Ask for local references and examples of recent installations.

Key questions to ask every contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and provide the results?
- What exact unit (brand/model/SEER) are you proposing and what size (tons)?
- What is included (permit, removal of old unit, refrigerant recovery, thermostat, line set, electrical upgrades, duct sealing)?
- What are parts and labor warranty lengths? Are there extended warranty options?
- Are technicians NATE-certified and employed (not subcontrators)?
- How long will the installation take and what is the payment schedule?
- Do you offer financing, rebates, or maintenance agreements?

What a good bid looks like
- Itemized written proposal with model numbers, SEER, capacity, efficiency ratings.
- Clear description of work (duct repair, new thermostat, electrical upgrades).
- Labor and parts warranties spelled out.
- Permit pulled and local code compliance included.
- Timeline and total price; removal and disposal of old equipment noted.

Typical cost ranges (Atlanta area, ballpark)
- Simple like-for-like replacement (smaller home, no duct work): roughly $4,000–$8,000.
- Higher-efficiency systems or larger homes: $6,000–$12,000+.
- If ducts need major work or home needs electrical upgrade, add more. (Get written estimates — prices vary widely.)

Red flags
- No written estimate or vague scope.
- Push to take cash only or immediate high deposit.
- No permits, unwillingness to provide references.
- Extremely low bid with pressure to sign right away.

If you want, give me your Atlanta zip code, system age/size, and whether you prefer a brand (Carrier, Trane, etc.) and I’ll suggest a short list of well-reviewed local companies and a sample message you can send to request bids.
